fatal_errors: The proposed dilute W addition to TiVNbTa does not reconstruct the target comparison between equiatomic CrFeTaVW and Ta-to-Ti-substituted CrFeTiVW.

The central target outcomes—chemical segregation, phase constitution after milling/SPS, and thermal diffusivity from 300 to 1000 K—are replaced by an unsupported mechanical-strength prediction at 1273 K.
Efficient heat transfer is asserted without predicting or measuring thermal diffusivity or conductivity; the target results actually show HEA diffusivity far below both W and CuCrZr.

Neither cited source supports the specific claim that 3–5 at.% W will produce greater than 450 MPa yield strength while retaining approximately 40% strain. E1 also highlights the risk of brittle W-enriched BCC phases.
The experiment does not directly test the proposed dislocation-climb or mobility mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad divertor-interlayer motivation and proposes a controlled baseline-versus-modified-alloy test, but it misses nearly every material-specific element of the hidden target. The target concerns Ta-to-Ti substitution in CrFeTaVW, hybrid MD/MC atom swaps, mechanical alloying and SPS, segregation and Laves/two-BCC phase formation, and thermal diffusivity. The generated answer instead proposes dilute W alloying of TiVNbTa and focuses on mechanical strength. Its quantitative strength and ductility predictions are extrapolations not established by the cited HEA evidence. The proposed experiment could falsify the strength and phase-stability claims, but it omits thermal transport and lacks measurements capable of distinguishing reduced dislocation climb from ordinary solid-solution strengthening or other microstructural effects.
